decision.what_is_decided: How to route one ACP agent JSON-RPC message: bookkeep streamed text or a tool_call, intercept a request for guarding, or only forward.

inputs.name: msg.id
inputs.role: marks a request that may be guarded

inputs.name: update subtype and content type
inputs.role: chooses intent accumulation vs tool_call memory

decision.downstream_action: Updates session maps and writes the original or a rejection onto the ACP pipes.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Branches compare protocol field values to fixed method and update names, not free-text meaning.

context_dependence.evidence: Routing does not use session history or user task; those are only stored for later guards.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Equality on method, id presence, sessionUpdate, and content type already encodes the dispatch.

judgment_required.evidence: No competing interpretations of the payload; each branch is a protocol case.

rule_stability.evidence: ACP method and update names are a wire contract, not a policy that drifts with wording.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Policy lives in guardRequest/assessAction; this function only dispatches.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Agent text is concatenated into intents, not classified.

decision_complexity.evidence: A few independent equality checks, then forward.

observed.claim: Dispatch is exact equality on ACP method and update fields.

evidence.observation: Handles session/update notifications by reading params.update and sessionId.
Appends chunk text only when sessionUpdate is agent_message_chunk and content type is text.
Records a tool_call when sessionUpdate is tool_call.
Requests with an id go through guardRequest; otherwise the message is forwarded.

inferred.claim: This is protocol plumbing; any semantic guard is delegated, not performed here.

evidence.observation: Request interception calls guardRequest rather than judging message text.
Natural-language chunks are stored, not interpreted.

unknown: Whether the developer ever considered Jev for classifying ACP update kinds.
Which other ACP methods they chose not to special-case.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: The Jev site judges free-text tool results; fromAgent only matches wire-protocol fields.

evidence.observation: scanContent asks noul/choice over truncated content and flags by kind and probability.
fromAgent branches on method, id, and sessionUpdate, then forwards.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Agent prose is buffered for later context, not classified as injection vs discussion.

evidence.observation: Text chunks are concatenated into intents.
scanContent maps kind and directed probability onto flagged vs not.

decision.what_is_decided: How to route one ACP client JSON-RPC message: record a prompt, resolve a permission reply, trigger a content scan, or only forward.

inputs.name: msg.id and absence of method
inputs.role: detects a response to a prior request

decision.downstream_action: Updates session memory and/or calls flagContent, then writes the message to the agent.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Conditions match fixed method names and the shape of a JSON-RPC response.

context_dependence.evidence: Scan vs skip here depends only on the remembered request method, not on content meaning.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: An allowlist of two result methods plus prompt/response shape fully specifies the routing.

judgment_required.evidence: No interpretation of prompt or file text occurs in this function.

rule_stability.evidence: ACP method names are a spec; adding a new scannable method would be an explicit allowlist edit.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Risk labeling is inside flagContent/scanContent; this only chooses when to call them.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Prompt text is sliced and stored; result text is passed through without reading it here.

observed.claim: Client-side handling is exact method and message-shape checks.

evidence.observation: session/prompt extracts text blocks, remembers a truncated prompt, and clears intents.
Responses with id and no method are matched to ours or agentReqs.
flagContent runs only when the original method is fs/read_text_file or terminal/output.

inferred.claim: Semantic injection judgment is intentionally deferred to scanContent, not done in the router.

evidence.observation: Only an allowlisted method pair triggers flagContent.
flagContent then calls scanContent or scanInstructionsCached on the result string.

unknown: Why only those two result methods are scanned in this proxy.
Whether other client methods were considered for scanning.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: fromClient decides whether to invoke the Jev scan by method name; scanContent decides what the text means.

evidence.observation: Equality on two ACP methods gates flagContent.
scanContent runs SCAN_QUESTIONS on content and computes flagged from kind and p.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Prompt text is stored as data, not classified as directed-at-AI.

evidence.observation: Text blocks are joined, truncated, and remembered.
The Jev site classifies content as injection, canary, discussion, benign, or unknown.

decision.what_is_decided: Whether a filesystem path is collected as an instruction or markdown file during a bounded recursive walk.

inputs.name: path
inputs.source: walk argument, starting from a root the caller supplies
inputs.role: subject of file vs directory and name tests

inputs.name: depth
inputs.role: caps descent and special-cases top-level markdown

outcomes: add path to the output set
decision.downstream_action: Fills a set of paths for later instruction scanning; does not read file bodies here.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Inclusion is path pattern, extension, depth, and skip-dir membership, not file meaning.

context_dependence.evidence: The same path at the same depth is always treated the same; no session or content context.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Instruction-file test, markdown-at-depth-0, MAX_DEPTH, and SKIP_DIRS are closed-form rules.

judgment_required.evidence: No competing labels for a path; it is collected or not.

rule_stability.evidence: Extension and skip-dir lists change only if the project adds new instruction locations.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Walk only discovers files; any untrusted-instruction policy is later, not here.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: File contents are not read in walk.

decision_complexity.evidence: Stat, two path tests, depth cap, skip-dir loop.

observed.claim: Collection is a path/stat filter with a depth bound.

evidence.observation: A file is added if it matches the instruction-file pattern or is markdown at depth 0.
Non-directories, over-depth dirs, and skip-listed names are not descended.

inferred.claim: This is discovery plumbing so later scanners know which files to read, not a semantic verdict on those files.

evidence.observation: Only the path string is tested; contents are unused.
Instruction-file paths elsewhere select a different scanner, showing path tests stay separate from Jev classification.

unknown: The full INSTRUCTION_FILE pattern and SKIP_DIRS set are not in this snippet.
Whether the developer considered judging file role from content instead of path.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: walk selects files by path shape; scanContent judges the meaning of already-loaded text.

evidence.observation: Adds a path using instruction-file or markdown-at-root tests.
Asks whether truncated content is AI-directed and of which kind.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: No competing semantic labels; outcomes are add, recurse, or skip.

evidence.observation: Control flow is stat, pattern, depth, and skip-dirs only.
The Jev site chooses among injection, canary, discussion, and benign.
